title: Hot-Kiln Glassblowing Shed
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk Bai Zhuo（Bai Zhuo, a glassblower around fifty, sunglasses-style goggles, fireproof apron, old burn scars on the arms） enters the glassblowing shed（Glassblowing shed: brick furnace mouth spraying orange fire, anvil and blowpipe rack side by side, air scorching） and first checks the blowpipe（A stainless-steel blowpipe, mouth faintly blue-hot, handle wrapped in hemp rope for grip, body carved with the character 'Zhuo'） on the rack.
A row of five heatproof goggles（A row of five heatproof goggles hung on shed iron hooks, lenses polished） hangs on the iron hooks; Bai Zhuo polishes each lens.
Two timekeeping bronze bells（Two timekeeping bronze bells hung in the kiln gallery, struck at shift change） hang in the kiln gallery; Bai Zhuo taps them lightly to test the ring.
Bai Zhuo circles the furnace mouth checking whether refractory bricks have peeled.
Through a kiln-gallery peephole Bai Zhuo watches the dull-red kiln fire.
The blowpipe mouth faintly blues; Bai Zhuo weighs it in his hand.
Bai Zhuo sits on an iron stool in the shed corner for a short rest.

Bai Zhuo opens the kiln-temperature notebook（A heat-resistant-covered kiln-temperature notebook recording furnace curves and color batches）—this heat-resistant cover record book—and copies the temperature gap between furnace mouth and annealing kiln.
With red and blue pens Bai Zhuo draws heat-up, hold, and anneal curve segments.
Bai Zhuo closes the record book and tucks it back into the locked iron box by the furnace.
The blowpipe sways lightly on the rack; Bai Zhuo nods.
Bai Zhuo wipes soot from the cover with a dry cloth and clips a temperature-test slip at the corner.

In the morning annealing kiln gallery（Annealing kiln gallery: annealing kiln doors in a long row, peepholes glowing dull red） Bai Zhuo greets young Ali（Apprentice Ali of fourteen or fifteen, indigo headscarf, gray fireproof vest, eyes clear and stubborn） pushing the material plank cart（An iron-frame material plank cart, bed loaded with quartz-sand bags, sides sprayed white with 'Zhuo Kiln'）.
Ali steadies the plank cart and restacks the quartz-sand bags.
Bai Zhuo points to the three cobalt-blue color rods（Three cobalt-blue color rods bound with iron wire on the rack, tips droplet-shaped） on the rack and teaches Ali to recognize the droplet tips.
Ali squats by a kiln door and curiously watches the peephole's red glow.
Bai Zhuo explains blow rhythm; Ali nods carefully.
Ali looks back at the iron-frame material plank cart, eyes full of tension.
Bai Zhuo has Ali first practice empty-tube blowing posture.

In the noisy glass market（Glass market: vases and bead ornaments under the awnings, sunlight fracturing into rainbow glints） Ayan（Young Ayan whose face closely resembles Ali's, but wearing a milky-white neckerchief and the same gray fireproof vest, manner bold） in a milky-white neckerchief looks up from behind a vase stall.
Ayan picks color beads at a bead stall; the neckerchief sways lightly.
Ayan haggles with the stall keeper, manner bold.
Ayan carries a paper box through the market crowd.
Ayan stops under the colored awning and looks back at the shed chimney.
In the annealing kiln gallery Ali and Ayan stand side by side—one indigo headscarf, one milky-white neckerchief.
Ali hands a color rod to Ayan; they check the tip together.
Ayan straightens Ali's indigo headscarf; they walk slowly along the kiln gallery.
Ali and Ayan part at the gallery end, heading to shed and market.
Heat washes past; their similar gray vests cross between kiln doors and separate again.
On a night months later Bai Zhuo alone tends the furnace in the glassblowing shed.

Bai Zhuo opens the kiln-temperature notebook（The same kiln-temperature notebook soaked through with soot, cover blackened, writing bled） and finds furnace-mouth ash has already blackened and wrinkled the heat-resistant cover.
Bai Zhuo wipes scorched marks from the blowpipe handle.
Bai Zhuo looks toward the pitch-black annealing kiln gallery.
The blowpipe gleams cold blue under the lamp; Bai Zhuo slowly turns the tube.
Bai Zhuo clips blotter paper onto the stained page and presses it under the measuring-tube iron rule.
In rainy season Bai Zhuo moves damp color rods onto the drying rack in the glassblowing shed.
Bai Zhuo brushes ash from inside the blowpipe with a soft brush.
At dawn Bai Zhuo checks kiln-door numbers in the annealing kiln gallery.
Bai Zhuo hangs a raincoat on a gallery pillar and listens to the furnace roar.
In high summer Bai Zhuo opens the shed skylight to drive out heat.
Bai Zhuo checks whether the furnace-temperature gauge needle is stuck.
When autumn wind rises Bai Zhuo gathers half-finished cover cloths outside the gallery.
Bai Zhuo trials a new cobalt color code on a blank notebook page.
On a frost night Bai Zhuo lights the emergency lamp and checks flashlight charge.
Bai Zhuo wraps sand bags in blankets against night damp.
On a heavy-snow day Bai Zhuo sweeps thin snow from the old kiln porch stone steps.
Bai Zhuo breathes on his hands and tightens the color-rod iron wire.
In early spring Bai Zhuo clears chimney ash.
Bai Zhuo disinfects the five pairs of goggles one by one.
Bai Zhuo posts a new shift roster on the shed wall.
Around Dragon Boat Festival Bai Zhuo smokes the materials store with mugwort against insects.
Bai Zhuo regrinds the droplet tips of the color rods round.
Bai Zhuo alone paces the kiln gallery, silently reciting blow beats.
After rain Bai Zhuo pushes open the shed door and listens to eaves water drip into an iron bucket.
Bai Zhuo swaps worn hemp rope for new.
On another dusk Bai Zhuo sits by the blowpipe listening to the furnace.
At night Bai Zhuo rises and feeds coal to the hearth.
Bai Zhuo sieves newly arrived quartz sand.
Bai Zhuo wipes the 'Zhuo Kiln' lintel on the porch.
Bai Zhuo checks the plank-cart hubs for cracks.
Bai Zhuo marks cup dimensions on a drawing.
Bai Zhuo wrings out ash-stained rags and hangs them.
On a full-moon night Bai Zhuo watches kiln fire from the gallery; peepholes like stars.
Bai Zhuo tidies the iron hooks so goggle straps hang down.
Bai Zhuo writes the new season's furnace notes inside the cover.
Bai Zhuo polishes the two timekeeping bronze bells bright.
Bai Zhuo hears market hawking and keeps stirring melt.
Bai Zhuo glues a cracked crucible support.
Bai Zhuo stacks cup blanks awaiting anneal in the shed corner.
Bai Zhuo closes the furnace door tight against a night temperature drop.
On another Qingming Bai Zhuo sets a bunch of wildflowers in the porch.
Bai Zhuo rolls drawings into a tube and binds them with a rubber band.
Bai Zhuo trials a low bronze-bell note; the sound is clear.
Bai Zhuo sits silent in the shed listening to melt bubble a long while.
Bai Zhuo cuts worn indigo cloth into rag stock.
Bai Zhuo shovels scorched slag from the flame mouth into an iron bucket.
At dawn Bai Zhuo patrols the annealing kiln gallery; the material plank cart rests at the gallery mouth.
Bai Zhuo crouches to check the plank-cart axle.
Bai Zhuo walks to the rack; those three cobalt-blue color rods are still bound with iron wire.

A blue electric forklift（A blue electric forklift, square body with no 'Zhuo Kiln' lettering—unlike the iron-frame plank cart） rolls past outside the gallery—square body, not the Zhuo Kiln plank cart.
Bai Zhuo stands in the kiln gallery and checks each kiln-door temperature with an infrared gun.
Bai Zhuo hangs wet canvas on the gallery rack.
Bai Zhuo brushes sand from his sleeves and looks back at the shed firelight.
After Grain Rain Bai Zhuo teaches a new apprentice in the kiln gallery to read peephole color temperature.
Bai Zhuo re-covers cup blanks with sun-dried cloths.
In summer heat Bai Zhuo lays a damp cloth on the blowpipe handle to cool it.
Bai Zhuo checks the plank cart and moves damp sand bags to the upper layer.
On an autumn night under the emergency lamp Bai Zhuo rethreads soot-stained record loose pages.
Bai Zhuo rotates the five pairs of goggles out for inspection.
At first snow Bai Zhuo sweeps a narrow path at the porch threshold.
Bai Zhuo rehangs the practice hollow tube on the rack.
Bai Zhuo hears the bronze bells ring lightly and continues editing the shift roster.
Bai Zhuo pushes open the gallery door so through-draft carries smoke away.
Bai Zhuo hangs rain canvas on the porch.
Bai Zhuo stores the cracked old tube section in an iron box.
At night Bai Zhuo dreams of furnace runaway; waking, he writes the reading beside the gauge.
Bai Zhuo rinses the color rack with clear water.
Bai Zhuo wipes the shift roster clean and reposts it.
Bai Zhuo pulls weeds from porch-pillar stone seams.
Bai Zhuo rehangs the goggles on iron hooks; number slips are somewhat faded.
Before lights-out Bai Zhuo takes a last look at the blowpipe wall.
Bai Zhuo folds the indigo headscarf an apprentice left in the shed.
Bai Zhuo hears the market closing horn and rises to lock up.
Bai Zhuo dries gloves by the warm box.
Bai Zhuo moves the bronze bells aside to show the newly repaired gallery beam.
Bai Zhuo air-dries temperature test chips.
Bai Zhuo draws a furnace-temperature comparison on the notebook's last page.
Bai Zhuo silently names tomorrow's cup shapes and steps out of the porch.
Bai Zhuo pushes the plank cart to the wall foot, clearing dip-ground.
Bai Zhuo hears a distant rooster and blows out the emergency lamp.
On another rain night Bai Zhuo alone tends the furnace fire until dawn.
Bai Zhuo weighs newly arrived cobalt color stock.
On a storm night furnace temperature spikes uncontrolled; shed alarms blare.
In the heat wave the anvil glows red-hot.
A sharp crack—the blowpipe（The same blowpipe with a cracked wall, air leaking on blow, hemp rope scorched）'s thin wall near the mouth splits; blown air leaks at once.
On the ramp outside the gallery the material plank cart loses control on the wet surface.
The material plank cart（The material plank cart tips on the ramp; frame twisted, sand bags split—wreckage） overturns; frame twists, sand bags split—utterly wrecked.
Bai Zhuo lunges at the rack and clamps hard on the cracked blowpipe.
A neighboring kiln master rushes with water; the shed fills with steam.
Next day Bai Zhuo stands in the glassblowing shed staring at the cracked blowpipe.
Bai Zhuo traces the wall crack with a finger, expression dark.
In a blank spot of the record book Bai Zhuo sketches the twisted frame and marks the date the material plank cart overturned.
An old photo of the material plank cart loaded with quartz sand still hangs on the wall; Bai Zhuo wipes the frame clean.
Bai Zhuo takes one of the five pairs of goggles from the iron hooks and puts them back on to check.
The cracked blowpipe still rests on the rack, scorched hemp marks clear.
Bai Zhuo sets wet boots at the door to drain.
Weeks later Bai Zhuo brings in a tube worker and cuts the cracked section off before the hemp-rope handle.

From a wooden crate Bai Zhuo takes a practice hollow tube（A practice hollow tube, shorter and lighter, no 'Zhuo' carving—much like a blowpipe but cannot enter the furnace） for comparison—shorter and lighter, no 'Zhuo' carving, and unable to take furnace heat.
The tube worker sleeves a liner into the new section; after the weld cools he rewraps the scorched hemp tight.

Replacement done, Bai Zhuo plugs the mouth and pressure-tests; the blowpipe（The blowpipe clear again after a new tube section is fitted; scorched hemp still wraps the handle, carved 'Zhuo' kept） is clear again, carved 'Zhuo' still there.
The repaired blowpipe gathers the first gather of glass; a clear bubble swells round.
Bai Zhuo redips into the furnace and turns the tube to blow a thin-walled small cup.

Outside the gallery comes sand merchant Old Shi（Sand merchant Old Shi, full beard, sand bag on the back, build like Bai Zhuo's but sturdier） with a quartz-sand bag on his back, build like Bai Zhuo's but without goggles.

The crafts supervisor（A lean crafts supervisor, white shirt with chest badge, build similar to Bai Zhuo's but more stiff） also arrives; white-shirt chest badge gleaming in the firelight, talking beside Bai Zhuo.
The supervisor points at the scrap-glass bin on the blue electric forklift and asks whether it belongs to the Zhuo Kiln plank cart.
The supervisor leaves; Bai Zhuo alone remains in the annealing kiln gallery.
Old Shi unloads a quartz-sand bag, bows farewell.
To the market comes a girl Xiaoni（Market girl Xiaoni in a light-brown headscarf, at a glance like young Ali, shy-eyed） in a light-brown headscarf—at a glance somewhat like young Ali.
Xiaoni tries sorting vases by mouth size; Bai Zhuo shakes his head—her light-brown headscarf is not Ali's indigo headscarf.
Xiaoni shyly lowers her head and ties the scarf tighter.

At dusk years later Bai Zhuo（The same Bai Zhuo: apron burned through, thick gauze on the forearm, walking slowly on an iron cane, goggles still hung on the chest） with gauze on the forearm leans on a cane in the old kiln porch（Old kiln porch: gray-brick porch, lintel carved 'Zhuo Kiln', scorched marks on the stone steps）.
Bai Zhuo looks up at the 'Zhuo Kiln' lintel, gaze distant.
Those two timekeeping bronze bells from the kiln gallery are brought to the porch for a test ring; Bai Zhuo stops to listen.
Bai Zhuo presses a palm to the porch's cold scorched brick as if saying goodbye.
Evening wind lifts a corner of his torn apron.
By day adult Ali（Ali in her twenties, still in the indigo headscarf, upright and steady） returns along the ramp and hurries toward the old kiln porch.
Under the porch Ali reunites with cane-leaning Bai Zhuo; they embrace.
By the rest-room cot Ali holds Bai Zhuo's hand.
Bai Zhuo（Bai Zhuo has left the post; only his fireproof apron and goggles remain in the shed—he himself no longer appears）'s breath grows weak; at last he closes his eyes and exits the post.
Ali folds Bai Zhuo's fireproof apron and sets it by the pillow.
Behind the shed door Bai Zhuo's goggles still hang; Ali reaches to stroke them gently.
On the porch pillar Ali stands before the newly nailed memorial iron plaque（A cast-iron memorial plaque nailed to the porch pillar, carved with Bai Zhuo's name and the kiln-opening year）.
Ali's fingertip traces Bai Zhuo's name carved on the iron plaque.
Ali sets a bunch of wildflowers beneath the iron plaque.
Ayan（Ayan after remaking his look still wears the milky-white neckerchief, manner deeper） with his remade look arrives from the market and tightly embraces Ali under the porch.
Ali and Ayan stand side by side in the porch—one quiet-eyed, one deep-mannered.
They look at each other in silence, watching similar faces.
Ayan tightens the milky-white neckerchief; Ali still wears the indigo headscarf.
The shot returns to years ago—that youth practicing empty-tube blowing in the kiln gallery appears again.
Opening furnace fire in the shed brightens again; a long blowing tube carved 'Zhuo' first blues at the mouth.
Flashback to that year's market—the milky-white-neckerchiefed gray-vest figure slips past.
That row of five heatproof eye shields on the iron hooks again reflects orange furnace light.
Back to that kiln-fire gallery of first meeting, peepholes dull red as before.
Again the image of those two old shift bells in the kiln gallery ringing lightly.
Ali carries that soot-stained furnace-temperature record book into the glassblowing shed.
On the rack those three cobalt-blue color rods are still bound with iron wire.
Ali takes the replaced-repaired blowpipe and turns her wrist into the furnace to redip.
New green rises again from porch stone seams.
Ali ties the indigo headscarf tight; dull-red light at the annealing kiln doors burns strong again.
